# Google Shopping

*Product* · also written Shopping tab

Google's shopping results and the Shopping tab, built from Merchant Center feeds and product markup.

Narrative: the topic [Shopping data: feeds, markup and Storebot](../topics/shopping-data.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

18 claims mention it: 4 from Google's documentation, 12 shown or said at the event (5 not in Google docs, 1 confirmed by Google docs, 5 consistent with Google docs, 1 nothing to verify), 2 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Free listings for products](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9199328?hl=en).

- [`D1-C342`](../sessions/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) Docs: Google's Inside Googlebot post (March 2026) says Googlebot is today just one user of a centralized crawling platform, and that dozens of other clients, such as Google Shopping and AdSense, send their crawl requests through the same infrastructure under other crawler names, with only the larger ones documented. `[D1-C342, docs, Search Central blog (31 March 2026), https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/03/crawler-blog-post]`
- [`D3-C347`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Docs: Google's Merchant Center help says products and details crawled from an online store can show up on Google even when they are not marked up with schema.org or added in Merchant Center, and lists the Shopping tab among the places Merchant Center free listings appear. `[D3-C347, docs, Google Merchant Center Help, https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9199328?hl=en]`
- [`D3-C389`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Docs: Google's crawler list says robots.txt rules addressed to the Storebot-Google user agent affect all surfaces of Google Shopping, such as the Shopping tab in Google Search. `[D3-C389, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/google-common-crawlers]`
- [`D3-C395`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Docs: Merchant Center's product_detail attribute takes up to 100 specifications, each a section name, attribute name and attribute value, and Google's help says clean key-value specifications improve product details on Google Shopping and AI-driven surfaces. `[D3-C395, docs, Google Merchant Center Help, https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9218260?hl=en]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D3-C353`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Schema.org product markup on websites is another source of billions of product offers for Google Shopping, next to merchant feeds. `[D3-C353, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C364`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Google Shopping said highly prescriptive product data is a lot of hard work for merchants and is no longer needed for LLMs. `[D3-C364, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C378`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Google Shopping called rich data with light structure the AI sweet spot: a little structure that helps the AI system understand the data, not deep, highly nested, complex structures. `[D3-C378, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C379`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Some structure is much better than none for AI systems, because without structure the model does not really know what is going on, Google Shopping said. `[D3-C379, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C406`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Google Shopping named the downside of adding Q&As and documentation to product markup: the page's markup becomes somewhat bigger. `[D3-C406, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C407`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google Shopping pointed to a Google holiday shopping blog post with early results from real merchants using the conversational attributes, and to the Merchant Center Help Center and schema.org for the attributes and properties. `[D3-C407, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C346`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: To appear in the Shopping tab of Google Search, a product must be submitted in Google Merchant Center; product structured data alone is not enough. `[D3-C346, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C356`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Behind the visible attributes, small pieces of product data such as brand and UPC or other barcodes are very important for Google Shopping's query understanding, retrieval and ranking. `[D3-C356, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C385`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google Shopping uses its own crawler, Storebot (Storebot-Google), instead of Googlebot because it needs fresh product information, prices, availability and shipping details and therefore crawls much more often. `[D3-C385, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C402`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Basic, well-specified product attributes such as price, brand and availability remain as important as ever for Google Shopping. `[D3-C402, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C405`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Web markup is an efficient and unambiguous way for sites to share product data with Google, Google Shopping said, repeating the Day 2 structured data talk. `[D3-C405, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C409`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, nothing to verify: Google Shopping described product data for AI as early days in a fast-moving area, with many more changes to come. `[D3-C409, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D3-C348`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Analysis: Google's free listings help says crawled store products can appear on Google without markup or Merchant Center but does not say whether that includes the Shopping tab; for a shop that wants Shopping tab visibility, the stage rule that Merchant Center is required is the safe working assumption. `[D3-C348, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C351`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Analysis: For an online shop, Product structured data is enough for product rich results and Google Images product annotations, but the Shopping tab needs a Merchant Center feed too; keep feed and markup values identical, since Google can use the markup to validate the feed. `[D3-C351, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-SHP-01` **SHOULD** · Documented: Use Product markup for rich results and a Merchant Center feed for the Shopping tab, with identical values (3 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SHP-02` **SHOULD** · Documented: Let Storebot-Google crawl product, cart and checkout pages, through robots.txt and bot protection (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
